Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. If you want to sell digital products but keep getting stuck at ‘WHAT would I actually sell?’ Start simple. 7 beginner-friendly ideas: ✨ Checklists ✨ Planners ✨ Trackers ✨ Canva templates ✨ Beginner guides ✨ Resource lists ✨ Workbooks But here's the part I'd pay most attention to: Don't create a random product just because you've seen somebody else selling it. Start with a PROBLEM. Who are you helping? What are they struggling with? What could make that problem quicker, easier or less overwhelming? Instead of: ‘I'll create a meal planner.’ Try: ‘I'll create a simple meal planner for busy women who don't have time to decide what to cook every night.’ Specific problem → specific person → more useful product.
